name: Release of Invalid Pointer or Reference
principle: Code releases memory with the wrong deallocator or passes a pointer/reference that is not valid for that deallocator. This can corrupt allocator state or memory and lead to crash or code execution.
detection_signals: free(ptr) where ptr was returned by new
delete ptr where ptr was returned by malloc/calloc/realloc/strdup
delete[] ptr where ptr was returned by new or malloc-family allocation
delete ptr where ptr was returned by new[]
free(ptr) after ptr = ptr + n, ptr++, or ptr += n from an allocated base
free(tok) or free(ap[i]) where tok/ap[i] comes from strtok, strsep, strchr, strstr, or pointer into another buffer
free(field) where field aliases a subobject/member address such as &obj.member or buf + offset
negative_signals: malloc/calloc/realloc/strdup result is released with free on the original stored base pointer
new result is released with delete on the same pointer value
new[] result is released with delete[] on the same pointer value
pointer traversal uses a separate cursor/index and free(base) releases the original allocation
token/subslice is copied with malloc/strdup/new before it is individually freed
std::unique_ptr, std::shared_ptr, std::vector, std::string, or RAII owner manages the allocation without manual free/delete
false_defense_traps: Checking ptr != NULL before free(ptr) does not make an interior or mismatched pointer valid
Casting before free/delete does not change the required matching allocator
Setting ptr = NULL after an invalid free does not prevent allocator corruption already caused
Allocator hardening may abort instead of preventing the bug
Freeing each strtok/strsep token is invalid because tokens point inside the original buffer
verification_focus: Does every release call use the matching deallocator on the exact original allocation pointer, not an interior pointer or alias?

consequence_chains.trigger: invalid release corrupts allocator metadata or adjacent memory
consequence_chains.consequence: memory corruption, crash, or possible arbitrary code execution

consequence_chains.trigger: allocation and release APIs are from incompatible families
released pointer was advanced into the allocation before deallocation
consequence_chains.consequence: invalid free, crash, or heap corruption

patch_principle: Use matching allocation and release pairs: malloc/calloc/realloc/strdup with free, new with delete, new[] with delete[].
Preserve the original allocation pointer and use separate cursor/index variables for traversal.
Do not free tokens, substrings, member addresses, or pointers into another allocation; free only the owning base allocation.
Prefer RAII containers and smart pointers such as std::unique_ptr, std::shared_ptr, std::vector, and std::string.
